Anycast

Contents

  • 1 History
  • 2 Applications
PurposeTo route traffic to the closest server
Introduction1989

Anycast is a network addressing and routing methodology in which a single destination IP address is shared by devices in multiple locations.

Routers direct packets to the topologically nearest member of the group, which is why the method underpins both root name servers and large content delivery networks.

History

[edit]

The technique was first formally described in 1993 by Craig Partridge, Trevor Mendez and Walter Milliken, who documented it as a way to reach the closest instance of a replicated service.

Figure 1. Visualization of anycast routing

Applications

[edit]

Anycast is used to distribute DNS root service, to absorb denial-of-service traffic across many sites, and to place cache nodes close to the users requesting them.
